description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of entity types identified in a biomedical named entity recognition (NER) task, likely from the study “From Zero to Hero: Harnessing Transformers for Biomedical Named Entity Recognition in Zero- and Few-shot Contexts.” The chart is divided into 24 distinct categories, each representing a different biomedical entity type, with percentages indicating their relative frequency. The largest segment, “Chemical,” dominates at 32% (blue), followed by “Protein” at 15% (orange), and “DNA” at 6% (green). Other notable categories include “Chemical Family,” “Disease,” and “Cell Type,” each at 5%; “Drug” at 4%; and “Frequency,” “Cell Line,” and “Dosage” each at 3%. Smaller segments (2% or less) include “Gene Or Gene Product,” “Strength,” “Form,” “Disease Or Phenotypic Feature,” “Reason,” “Route,” “Chemical Entity,” “Sequence Variant,” “Modifier,” “RNA,” “Disease Class,” “Organism Taxon,” “Duration,” “ADE,” and “Composite Mention,” with several of these occupying just 1% or less. The chart uses a vibrant, multi-color palette to distinguish each category, with labels placed outside the pie and connected by lines for clarity. The visual emphasizes the overwhelming prevalence of “Chemical” entities, followed by a long tail of more specialized or less frequent entity types, reflecting the domain-specific focus and distribution of biomedical text annotations.
